outcome: mean cost per woman and infant(s)
cohort: Women with late preterm pre-eclampsia between 34+0 and 36+6 weeks' gestation from 46 maternity units in England and Wales were randomized to either planned delivery or expectant management.
finding: Planned delivery resulted in significantly lower mean costs per woman and infant(s) over 24 months and has a high probability of being cost-effective compared to expectant management for late preterm pre-eclampsia.
